question: With exact, zero-noise counterfactual labels at every armable state, can a small observable-feature policy select options profitably on held maps, closed-loop?
verdict_meaning: Phase 0-2 all PASS (label pipeline byte-exact; corpus generated; signal floor cleared 5x over). Phase 3 (fits + LOBO selection) admitted 0/4 fits -- every fit's decisive failure is the LOBO pooled-mean gate (all land +0.14..+0.26 vs the +1.5 floor). Per the protocol's pre-adjudicated decision tree, this is the terminal outcome: Phase 4 (veto panel, sealed confirmation) was never executed. This CLOSES the dense-counterfactual-credit route and, per the protocol text, constitutes the final closure of the Tier-2 learning route over this option vocabulary.

phase0_label_pipeline_validation.gate: recompute >=32-(task,arm) sample of D169a's consumed-panel arm values byte-exact
phase0_label_pipeline_validation.result: PASS: 256/256 rows byte-exact (own_score, opponent_score, action_hash, state_hash) against BOTH d169a-jobs1 and d169a-jobs20 bulk TSVs (8x the 32-sample floor)
phase0_label_pipeline_validation.extended_defensive_check_not_a_gate: Cross-checked scan_task's 81-field feature vectors against the live tf_d170a_* FFI (D170aVecEnv, all-KEEP). Found and fixed two real bugs before they could contaminate the corpus: (1) resource _trig arms offered one turn late (copied D170b's env-specific sticky-flag workaround instead of D169a's own same-turn native timing -- caught by the PRIMARY gate itself); (2) decisions_seen_so_far (state field 62) computed once per simultaneous-candidate group instead of incremented per candidate within the group (caught by the extended check). After both fixes: 0 mismatches on the primary gate; the only remaining extended-check mismatches (63/639, all isolated to opt_*_trig candidates as complete groups) are the deliberate, already-validated same-turn-vs-D170a's-turn+1 divergence, not a residual defect.

phase1_training_corpus.seed_range: 9,860,000-9,860,511 (512 fresh maps x 8 families x 2 seats = 8,192 tasks)
phase1_training_corpus.pre_lock_seed_overlap_grep: CLEAR (zero hits in both ledger volumes and all docs/**/*.md outside the D172a protocol/lock themselves; sealed ranges 9,844,200-215 / D164 field games / D170's 9,850,000-9,852,063 all numerically disjoint)

phase2_signal_floor.frozen_floor: >=8% of armable states have max-option label >= +2.0, present in both seats and >=6 families
phase2_signal_floor.result: PASS at 40.4% (5x the 8% floor); both seats; all 8/8 families

phase3_fits_and_selection.training: Huber loss (delta=1.0), Adam lr=1e-3, 200 epochs, batch 4096, one deterministic thread/fit; all hyperparameters frozen before any Phase 3 outcome was observed
phase3_fits_and_selection.weight_export_crosscheck: PyTorch model output vs Python parse+matmul of the exported Rust-consumable weights.txt: max_abs_diff=1.07e-6 over 20 sampled rows x 13 heads -- export format verified correct
phase3_fits_and_selection.thread_parity: 1 vs 20 threads byte-identical row digests (linear/172101, 8-map sample)

common_to_all_4_fits.crop_workforce_safety_exact: PASS in all 4 (zero purity violations / invalid direct commands / provenance failures)
common_to_all_4_fits.catastrophes_le_control: PASS in all 4 (49 policy vs 49 control, every fit)

phase3_fits_and_selection.decision: 0/4 admitted -> CLOSED-AT-SELECTION per the frozen decision tree

phase4_veto_and_confirmation.reason: Per the protocol's pre-adjudicated decision tree, Phase 4 only runs after Phase 3 admits a fit. 0/4 admitted, so veto and confirmation were never run.
phase4_veto_and_confirmation.veto_panel_status: untouched (D169a/D170a/D170b's consumed 1,024-task panel, seeds 9,844,136-9,844,199) -- still veto-only for a future dispatch

interpretation.signal_vs_selection_gap: Phase 2 proved dense positive signal exists at a rate an order of magnitude above the kill floor (40.4% vs 8%), and Phase 0's byte-exact labels rule out D153-D156-style regression-target noise. Phase 3 shows the two frozen function classes CAN extract and act on some of that signal (small but consistently positive, non-zero pooled means of +0.14..+0.26, activation rates 4-10%, concentrated almost entirely on the least-negative-always-on arm family (opt_fruit_*), essentially zero selection of the strongly-negative-always-on arms (opt_iron/opt_return) -- a mechanistically sensible pattern, not noise) but the achieved value is roughly an order of magnitude short of the +1.5 admission bar, and at least one of the 8 held LOBO blocks is net-negative for every fit. This is qualitatively different from D170b's on-policy closed-loop result (100% collapse to always-KEEP, pooled_mean exactly 0.0 in all 8 fits, P(invoke)<=3.3%): here, with exact labels, the models genuinely learn to invoke a meaningful minority of the time and do so with real (if small) positive expected value -- confirming the underlying decision problem IS learnable to a first approximation from these features under supervision, unlike the on-policy regime. But 'learnable to a first approximation with the wrong magnitude' is not the same as 'clears the value bar'; the frozen protocol's admission threshold treats this correctly as a non-admission, not a partial pass.
interpretation.does_not_answer: Whether a larger/different function class, more corpus, or a different (non-frozen-post-outcome) tau could clear the bar -- the protocol explicitly prohibits retuning after this outcome is seen; any such follow-on is a NEW program requiring its own authorization, per the same house rule D170b's own closure was recorded under.
